shared_elements: low-relief carving on pale weathered stone
a band of closely spaced short vertical strokes or repeated marks
animal or creature figures in profile
vertical flanking/framing elements (pilaster-like edges in A, pillar shaft edges in B)
justification: Both surfaces organise low relief into stacked horizontal registers filled with rows of repeated small motifs, and both are framed by vertical raised edges, which is the most specific correspondence. The decisive difference is legibility and scale of execution: B shows crisp, plastically modelled animals, birds and a fringe-like band on a narrow free-standing pillar, whereas A is a broad wall whose carving is so eroded that only faint horizontal traces survive, making its imagery essentially unreadable.
